description: We are Infinite Thinkers, a passionate team participating in the NASA Space Apps Challenge. We aim to combine creativity, science, and technology to solve real-world problems using NASA’s open data. We welcome curious and motivated members interested in space science, coding, AI/ML, data science, research, UI/UX design, and presentations. We value teamwork, ideas, and willingness to learn. Together we'll explore possibilities, develop meaningful solutions, and push boundaries beyond Earth!
summary:
SkyShift is a Streamlit-based prototype for exploring NASA SPHEREx infrared spectral-image observations and preparing same-sky-region comparisons over time. The application lets users inspect local FITS files, examine metadata and science-image headers, search candidate SPHEREx observations around a sky position through the NASA/IPAC Infrared Science Archive (IRSA), and play an exploratory sequence from previously downloaded observations.

SkyShift supports the Planet X and SPHEREx challenge by providing a transparent workflow for identifying, inspecting, and organizing candidate SPHEREx observations. It includes challenge-target presets, coordinate-based archive searching, FITS visualization, reprojection support, sequence playback, and an experimental image-difference screening tool. A clearly labeled Planet X simulation demonstrates the intended comparison workflow without presenting synthetic content as real evidence.

The project emphasizes scientific caution: image playback or pixel differences do not establish motion, variability, or object identity. Real temporal analysis requires compatible wavelengths, astrometric alignment, calibration review, and documented uncertainty. SkyShift makes these limitations visible to users while offering an accessible interface for exploratory infrared-sky investigation.
details:
SkyShift is a Python and Streamlit web application for exploratory inspection of NASA SPHEREx spectral-image data. Users can select local FITS files or upload observations, inspect 2D science extensions and FITS headers, adjust display contrast, and view image metadata. The application also provides a coordinate-search interface that constructs an ADQL query for the IRSA SPHEREx ObsCore catalog and requests candidate observations around a user-defined sky position.

The app includes challenge-target presets for WISE 0855, Barnard’s Star, Epsilon Indi B, RW Aurigae, and R Draconis. These presets fill coordinate fields for archive searching; they do not themselves confirm target coverage, identify an object, or validate an observation sequence. The interface clearly states that catalog coordinates may refer to an earlier epoch and that fast-moving sources require epoch-dependent position checks.

SkyShift includes an aligned sequence inspector for exploratory playback of downloaded FITS cutouts, a metadata table, and an experimental screening module that computes a robust median-centered image difference and quality indicators. It also includes a clearly labeled Planet X simulation for demonstrating the proposed comparison workflow. The simulation is synthetic and is not evidence of a real astronomical detection.

The project uses Python, Streamlit, Astropy, NumPy, Matplotlib, Pandas, Photutils, scikit-learn, and requests. It accesses SPHEREx Quick Release spectral images and metadata through NASA/IPAC IRSA. During testing, the live IRSA TAP endpoint returned an HTTP 502 proxy error; SkyShift explicitly reports this as an external archive-service issue rather than treating it as an astronomical result. Previously downloaded observations remain available for offline inspection and exploratory playback.

The intended impact is to make SPHEREx data exploration more approachable while maintaining scientific transparency. SkyShift is designed to help users organize candidate observations, inspect raw FITS products, understand observational limitations, and prepare for more rigorous temporal analysis. Its creative contribution is combining accessible visualization, target presets, provenance-aware experimental screening, and an explicit simulation mode in one educational interface.
